sourceFirstFindings.conditions: The 180 EC Compas pathway comprises 156 EC of compulsory major study, including the 6 EC thesis, and a 24 EC minor. The existing 27 components retain 60 EC in each year. Amsterdam Global Health is the first-listed faculty minor, selected neutrally; it studies local primary/community care, social determinants, diversity and participatory projects. It is a minor choice, not a graduation specialization, and selection, capacity and annual availability apply. External minors require approval, a coherent nonoverlapping university programme of at least 24 EC, at most 6 EC at level 100 and at least 12 EC at level 300; placements cannot fill this minor. The additional 6 EC minor thesis applies only to visiting non-Medicine students and is not added here. Year-2 entry requires the first-year study-advice threshold of 42 EC. Year-3 entry requires all Year 1 and 30 EC from Year 2; minor entry additionally requires at least 18 EC from semester 2.1. Care-placement preparation must be passed or equivalent knowledge accepted by the examiner. General-practice placement requires sufficient professional behavior in the care placement and approval by the Medical Expert examiner. Confidentiality must be signed before patient-related teaching. Practical work, study groups and placements require attendance and participation. The Dutch diagnostic/remedial language pass gates Doctor and Patient 1; professional behavior, portfolios, immediate knowledge, skills/first-aid and final progress assessments are embedded pass conditions, not extra credit units. Embedded research introductions belong to Doctor and Patient 2/4; general-practice work belongs to Medical Expert 4 within Doctor and Patient 4. The care placement carries 6 EC once. The compulsory thesis is the nonexempt final work of the major, after the minor in semester 3.1. Current course guidance specifies a short systematic review or, for research-minor students, a report of their own study: about 3000–5000 words in scientific English, an initial proposal, individual supervision and weekly meetings/writing sessions. Students arrange and register a suitable supervisor and tentative subject before their course starts, using Canvas instructions. The current January 2027 registration date concerns current Year-3 students; it is not imposed on the Fall 2026 entrant’s future Year 3. The thesis is graded at least 6.0 after all obligations are met. This comparison uses the 2026–2027 Compas rules for Fall 2026 entrants. VUMED360 starts in September 2027 and cannot absorb Compas credits. The last full teaching years are 2026–2027 for Year 1, 2027–2028 for Year 2 and 2028–2029 for Year 3; no regular Compas teaching follows August 2029. The final graduation deadline is 31 August 2030. The transition appendix governs remaining assessments and exceptional opportunities; it also provides an individual delayed-study-advice decision for affected entrants. Later annual offerings and minor placement must be checked.

concepts: Investigate human function, molecular and organ-system disease, pharmacology, brain function and the psychological experience of illness, using laboratory, statistical and research-synthesis methods. This offers substantial biomedical and psychological study related to Medicine, while patient examination, clinical reasoning in practice and medical professional formation remain outside the programme.

Retain substantial biomedical study while investigating health risks, social influences on illness, diversity, rights and community participation. Population-health evidence, qualitative inquiry and a civil-society project support this direction; rights and sociology are specific social complements, not clinical care or specialist health-law training.
substantiveChallenge.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each programme: neurobiology, higher cognitive functions, psychodiagnostics/psychotherapies and lifespan psychology are replaced by social psychology, qualitative research, contemporary social theory and human rights. These changes implement the social-inclusion concept rather than arbitrary breadth.
substantiveChallenge.stopping: Two distinct qualified responses are supported by the verified biomedical/psychological core and the exact-target diversity/population-health direction, including the selected minor’s social determinants and community-research content. The second changes four courses/30 EC toward social psychology, qualitative methods, civil society and rights. Supervised patient-contact learning cannot be supplied by academic anatomy, laboratory cases or psychodiagnostics; that candidate remains not feasible. No third programme is manufactured from postgraduate careers or illustrative activities.

result: All academic, mechanical and actual desktop/mobile presentation gates passed against the frozen inputs; suitable for final approval after durable evidence publication.
